title: Mechanisms of Projective Composition of Diffusion Models
role: The theory of when adding scores is exact, used to test whether a right-minus-wrong sentence score could qualify
reads: Exact scores of noised distributions in theory; CLEVR experiments use an EDM2 U-Net on 128 by 128 images conditioned on one location or colour
trained_on: CLEVR: 50,000 empty scenes, 1,550,000 single-object scenes, 2,500,000 scenes with 1 to 5 objects; no text and image critic
score_enters: Background score plus the sum of expert-minus-background score differences at every reverse-diffusion step, unit coefficients, no cap (Eq. 6 and Eq. 8)
adding_scores: Exact when coordinates split into blocks where each expert differs from an independent background only on its own block (Def 5.2, Thm 5.3); feature-space version has no sampling guarantee unless the map is orthogonal; a right-minus-wrong push fails these conditions when the base mixes right and wrong (inferred)
properties: Counting and position measured on CLEVR; binding, spatial relation, size and prompt match not tested
unseen: no: tests more objects than any single model saw, with no held-out concepts
headline: Largest working object count 4 with an empty background against 1 with an unconditional background, models trained on 1 object, CLEVR, EDM2 U-Net
copy_or_avoid: Copy the mean-difference orthogonality check and read the and-score as what the score sum omits; avoid citing Theorem 5.3 or 6.1 for swap-pair pushes (inferred)
model: EDM2 U-Net on CLEVR; SDXL for two example figures
